# Jev DevTools

> React request inspector for TypeSafe Jev, with a Node server adapter. Development-only opt-in; React 18/19, Node 22.12+. Custom drawer; TanStack Virtual is used internally for Questions.

## Set up in an existing app

- [Setup skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/diegoag64/jev-devtools/main/packages/jev-devtools/skills/setup-jev-devtools/SKILL.md): Start here; selects the framework and defines a complete integration.
- [React / Node / Vite](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/diegoag64/jev-devtools/main/packages/jev-devtools/skills/setup-jev-devtools/references/react-node.md): Root drawer, middleware, proxy, local Vite option.
- [Next.js App Router](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/diegoag64/jev-devtools/main/packages/jev-devtools/skills/setup-jev-devtools/references/nextjs.md): Shared server adapter, optional catch-all route, client boundary.
- [Verification and troubleshooting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/diegoag64/jev-devtools/main/packages/jev-devtools/skills/setup-jev-devtools/references/verify.md): No-key sample, captured request, SSE, production behavior.

The skill and references ship in npm at `node_modules/jev-devtools/skills/setup-jev-devtools/`. Prefer the installed version's guidance and declaration files when it differs from main. These are explicit entry points, not a promise of automatic discovery by every AI tool.

## Build connected flows (0.4.0)

- [Bundled flow recipe](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/diegoag64/jev-devtools/main/packages/jev-devtools/skills/setup-jev-devtools/references/flows.md): Agent workflow for requests, tasks, runtime factories, parallel lanes, branches, returning conditionals, maps and loops; scope rules, sample checks and troubleshooting. Available offline beside the installed setup skill.
- [Flow API guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/diegoag64/jev-devtools/main/docs/flows.md): Definition versus execution, typed references, conditions, joins, errors/cancellation, recording and viewer limits.

Use the installed `lib/flow/index.d.ts` as the version-matched API contract. Define on Node; execute with the shared instrumented client and inspector. Existing request capture does not require adopting flows. Do not invent thresholds or business actions.

## 0.4.0 capabilities and examples

The 0.4.0 flow API includes `task()`, runtime `jev()` request factories, `.answers`, `map()`, `if()`, strict `.gt()` comparisons, and `loop()`. Loops check a state expression before each iteration and reject incomplete iteration-limit exhaustion with `FlowLoopLimitError`. A loop can contain a map; all expanded work shares one run-wide budget. There are no nested loops, loops inside maps, nested maps, durable jobs, or automatic task retries. Use installed declarations and bundled references for the exact version; check the changelog for publication status.

- [Cookbook collection](https://github.com/diegoag64/jev-devtools/blob/main/cookbooks/README.md): Six runnable repository apps using the 0.4.0 APIs. Code and synthetic fixtures are not shipped in npm.
- [SDE cascade](https://github.com/diegoag64/jev-devtools/blob/main/cookbooks/sde-cascade/README.md): Sample-only returning conditional, strict escalation gate and shared continuation.
- [Hierarchical classification](https://github.com/diegoag64/jev-devtools/blob/main/cookbooks/hierarchical-classification/README.md): Bounded iteration, frontier collections, beam versus greedy search and iteration-limit failure.
- [Structure Recovery](https://github.com/diegoag64/jev-devtools/blob/main/cookbooks/structure-recovery/README.md): Tasks, dynamic requests and returning conditionals; four sample-only cases.
- [Simple Memory](https://github.com/diegoag64/jev-devtools/blob/main/cookbooks/simple-memory/README.md): Tasks, dynamic requests, conditionals and loops; four sample-only timelines with customer-scoped run-local memory and an inclusive 50% save gate. No persistent storage.
